questions.stem: The 'weight' of an oil refers to its:
questions.explanation: Use the grade the manufacturer specifies.

questions.stem: Milky oil on a diesel engine's dipstick usually indicates:
questions.explanation: Report and investigate. A failed head gasket or cooler may be letting water in.

options: Can be mixed in any ratio
questions.explanation: They have different additives and properties. Follow the manufacturer's specification.

options: Stored in a sealed container and disposed of at an approved facility
questions.explanation: Never discharge oil. It is illegal and harms the environment.

questions.stem: Besides reducing friction, a lubricating oil in an engine also:
options: Cools, cleans, seals and protects against corrosion
Only fills gaps and adds weight
Stops water entering through the exhaust
questions.explanation: Oil carries heat away, holds dirt for the filter, seals piston rings and coats metal surfaces.

questions.stem: An oil is marked 15W-40. The 15W part tells you:
options: Its thickness at full running temperature
How well it flows when cold, where a lower number flows more easily
The percentage of additive in it
questions.explanation: The number before the W describes cold flow. The second number describes thickness when hot.

questions.stem: The correct way to check an engine's oil level is to:
options: Read the dipstick while the engine is running at idle
Fill until oil shows at the filler cap
Stop the engine, let the oil settle, then read the dipstick and keep the level between the marks
Read it once and add a litre to be safe
questions.explanation: A running engine holds oil away from the sump, so the reading is false. Between the marks is correct.

questions.stem: Why is overfilling an engine with oil harmful?
options: It makes the oil run cooler
The crankshaft whips the oil into foam, which lubricates poorly and can push oil past seals
It raises the fuel consumption only
questions.explanation: Aerated oil gives poor pressure and a weak film.

questions.stem: A low oil pressure alarm sounds on a running engine. The correct first action is to:
options: Increase engine speed to raise pressure
Stop the engine, then look for the cause
Finish the passage and check later
questions.explanation: Bearings can fail within minutes without oil pressure. Stop first, investigate second.

questions.stem: The dipstick oil smells strongly of diesel, looks thin, and the level has risen. This most likely indicates:
options: Fuel dilution, for example from a leaking injector or lift pump
questions.explanation: Fuel dilution thins the oil and raises the level. Water would make it milky instead.
